To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a diet with 30% protein, 40% carbohydrate and 30% fat, compared to a 20% protein, 55% carbohydrate and 25% fat diet, results in a greater weight loss in the short-term and a greater fat loss in the long-term, but not a greater loss of fat free mass.
the diet with the highest amount of protein (30%) was the best diet for weight maintenance, followed by the 25% protein diet, and then the 15% protein diet.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a diet with a high protein, low carbohydrate, and low fat composition, when compared with a low protein, high carbohydrate, and moderate fat diet, is more effective at inducing weight loss, improving metabolic health, and maintaining the weight loss in overweight and obese individuals.
a diet that is low in fat and high in carbohydrates (low-fat, high-carbohydrate diet) is the best for weight loss.
a high-protein diet is effective for weight loss and maintenance, especially when the diet is high in unsaturated fat, low in refined carbohydrate, and low in energy density.

a low carbohydrate diet, in this case, a low glycemic index diet, can lead to weight loss and weight loss maintenance.
the diet composition matters when it comes to weight loss and maintenance.
